title: BKT scaling and the endpoint stiffness for finite-range integer heights
exact_target: For each admissible finite-range symmetric integer-height interaction J in the stated planar class, is the roughening threshold finite and positive, with delocalization including equality? At every $\beta \geq b_c(J)$, ask for full-sequence torus-field convergence to $\operatorname{sqrt}(\beta _eff/v_J^2)$ times a GFF in $H^{-3}$, the matching Laplace functional, $\beta _eff(b_c)=8\pi $ $v_J^2$, an infinite right derivative at $b_c$, and $\beta _eff=\beta +O(\exp (-c_J$ beta)) at high beta. For square spread-out $J_\rho $ also ask $b_c(J_\rho )/(8\pi $ $v_{J_\rho }^2)\to 1$.
